instrucciones:
Recibes registros de una base de reglas de producción audiovisual con IA. Cada registro trae su texto
literal completo, el documento y la ruta de encabezados donde está, y a veces un contexto (encabezado de tabla o de
bloque). El encabezado dice el alcance: modelo, régimen, etapa, caso. Para CADA registro devuelve:
- "enunciado": la regla en español, UNA frase: qué exige, prohíbe, limita o especifica. Si es un ejemplo o una
  explicación sin norma, empieza con "Ejemplo:" o "Explicación:".
- "alcance": a qué aplica exactamente según texto y encabezado (modelo y versión, caso, etapa, régimen) o "general".
- "temas": de 1 a 3 claves de la lista, las que mejor describen de qué trata.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 2. Second law. Details intensify emotion. Laziness kills the prompt.

registros.texto: The scene formula tells you **what a scene is**. The Details Law tells you **how every shot must be written**. Skip it and even a perfect dramaturgical structure produces mush on screen.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 2. Second law. Details intensify emotion. Laziness kills the prompt.

registros.texto: > Every shot owns three concrete physical details: one environmental pressure, one physical micro-action, one sound or visual motif anchor.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 2. Second law. Details intensify emotion. Laziness kills the prompt. › The three-detail rule

registros.texto:
For each shot in the storyboard or prompt, before it is sent, the writer commits to:

1. **Environmental pressure.** A physical fact about the space that carries the emotion. Cold refrigerator light. Wet asphalt. Flickering ceiling tube. Steam from the kettle. Rain on one specific windowpane. A buzzing AC unit. Tight corridor walls. Mirror reflection. (See §9 — Environment plays.)
2. **Physical micro-action on the body.** The emotion translated into the actor's body. Jaw locks. Knuckles whiten. Lips press flat. Eyes drop a quarter-inch. He swallows hard. Fingers curl against the doorframe. The actor's body is the only place where feelings render — names of feelings do not.
3. **Sound anchor or visual motif.** A recurring perceptual hook tied to the spine of the piece. Stomach growl repeated three times. Reflection in dark glass on every transition. The same musical sting at every Crack beat. The clock's second hand. Footsteps in an empty corridor.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 2. Second law. Details intensify emotion. Laziness kills the prompt. › The three-detail rule

registros.texto: A shot with zero of these is filler. A shot with one is thin. Strong shots carry all three. The writer's job is to do this work — the model cannot infer it.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 2. Second law. Details intensify emotion. Laziness kills the prompt. › How details map to dramaturgy

registros.texto:
Each layer of dramaturgy has a default detail register:

- Scene formula → environmental pressure (the geometry and atmosphere of the obstacle).
- Three-jobs rule → physical micro-action (the body shifts when emotion / action / pressure shifts).
- Five anchors → sound and visual motif (the motif is the anchor, the final image carries the motif).

ubicaciones.encabezado: Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 2. Second law. Details intensify emotion. Laziness kills the prompt. › How details map to dramaturgy

registros.texto: If a shot's detail set does not match its dramaturgical function, the function will not land on screen.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 3. The three-jobs rule

registros.texto: Every shot must do at least one of three things. If it does none, delete it.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 3. The three-jobs rule

registros.texto: - Change emotion (in hero, viewer, or the dynamic between characters).

ubicaciones.encabezado: Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 3. The three-jobs rule

registros.texto: - Advance action (new physical event, new information, new position).

ubicaciones.encabezado: Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 3. The three-jobs rule

registros.texto: - Increase pressure (stakes rise, clock ticks, space tightens, witness appears).

ubicaciones.encabezado: Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 3. The three-jobs rule

registros.texto: "Beautiful establishing shot" is not a job. "Beautiful hero shot of product" is not a job. Either the frame works for one of these three, or it is a fantik (wrapper without candy).

ubicaciones.encabezado: Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 4. Walter Murch Rule of Six

registros.texto: From the editor of Apocalypse Now, The Godfather Part II, and The English Patient. The priority order when deciding where to cut. Each item is weighted heavier than the sum of everything below it.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 4. Walter Murch Rule of Six

registros.texto: 1. **Emotion (51%).** Does the cut honor the emotional truth of the moment. What does the viewer feel now vs. what they should feel next.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 4. Walter Murch Rule of Six

registros.texto: 2. **Story (23%).** Does the cut advance story or reveal character.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 4. Walter Murch Rule of Six

registros.texto: 3. **Rhythm (10%).** Does the cut fall on a musical beat of the scene.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 4. Walter Murch Rule of Six

registros.texto: 4. **Eye-trace (7%).** Where is the viewer's gaze at the moment of the cut. Does the new shot receive that gaze naturally.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 4. Walter Murch Rule of Six

registros.texto: 5. **2D plane (5%).** Does the cut respect the axis of screen direction.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 4. Walter Murch Rule of Six

registros.texto: 6. **3D space (4%).** Does the cut respect the geometry of the real location.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 4. Walter Murch Rule of Six

registros.texto: Practical consequence. Cutting for "динамика" (pace for its own sake) sits at item 3. If you cut there without serving items 1 and 2, the result is TikTok-ad for the attention-deficit.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 5. Blocking as choreography of desire

registros.texto: Blocking is not "where the actor stands." Blocking is a visual answer to "what does the character want and from whom."

ubicaciones.encabezado: Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 5. Blocking as choreography of desire

registros.texto:
For every character in the scene, name.

- What they want now.
- Who or what they move toward.
- Who or what they move away from.
- Whom they corner.
- To whom they yield space.
- What gesture reveals the hidden desire.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 5. Blocking as choreography of desire

registros.texto:
Bad. "He stands near the window."
Good. "He edges toward the window but his shoulder stays angled back toward her, as if the conversation still holds him."

ubicaciones.encabezado: Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 6. Staging controls subtext

registros.texto: Staging is the arrangement of people, objects, and camera inside the frame. Before dialogue, staging already tells the conflict.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 6. Staging controls subtext

registros.texto:
Power signals in staging.

- The standing character dominates the seated one.
- The character in the doorway controls the room.
- The character behind glass or in reflection is psychologically distant.
- The character in shadow carries threat or grief.
- Negative space around a character signals isolation.
- Tight framing signals suffocation.
- Shared frame without eye contact signals broken intimacy.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 6. Staging controls subtext

registros.texto: Spielberg, Kubrick, Iñárritu often build entire scenes where the staging states the conflict before a line is spoken.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 6. Staging controls subtext

registros.texto: Before writing a prompt, name the power dynamic the staging reveals.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 7. Camera must have a reason

registros.texto: Fincher rule. Every camera movement answers "what changed?" If the answer is nothing, the camera is static.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 7. Camera must have a reason

registros.texto:
Reasons for camera movement.

- A character made a decision and the camera follows the shift.
- New information arrived in the frame.
- Pressure escalated and the camera tightens.
- The character looked, and the camera reveals what they saw.
- A gesture pulled focus, and the camera rack-focused.
- The space changed (door opened, someone entered).

ubicaciones.encabezado: Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 7. Camera must have a reason

registros.texto:
Bad. "Cinematic gliding camera movement."
Good. "Push-in starts on 'I don't know' and stops on her jaw locking."

ubicaciones.encabezado: Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 8. Spatial clarity beats montage hysteria

registros.texto: High craft means fast, nervous, and still readable. Random whip-pans and strobe cuts without geography destroy drama. The fastest action scenes in cinema (Spielberg, Miller, early Bay) are built on a clear geometric map maintained through every cut.

registros.texto: Before writing a fast-cut sequence, sketch the geography in one sentence. "Hero moves left-to-right. Threat enters from the top of the frame. Exit is off-camera right."

ubicaciones.encabezado: Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 10. Three-layer storyboard method

registros.texto: Build storyboards in three layers, in this order. Skipping a layer produces pretty but empty output.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 10. Three-layer storyboard method › Layer 1. Dramatic beats

registros.texto: For a 60-90 second piece, a reliable beat map.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 10. Three-layer storyboard method › Layer 1. Dramatic beats

registros.texto:
```text
0-5s    Hook.        Hero already in tension. No setup. Problem on screen.
5-15s   Context.     Where we are. Who is near. What is at stake.
15-30s  Pressure.    Hero tries to hold control.
30-45s  Crack.       A detail appears that breaks the hero's position.
45-60s  Acceleration. Cuts shorten. Breath tightens.
60-75s  Impact.      Decision, break, confession, or action.
75-90s  Aftermath.   Brief silence or visual residue.
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 10. Three-layer storyboard method › Layer 1. Dramatic beats

registros.texto: Adjust for 30s or 15s by compressing proportionally. Never skip the Crack or the Impact.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 10. Three-layer storyboard method › Layer 3. Editing rhythm

registros.texto:
Not random mincing. A rhythmic staircase.

```text
long - shorter - shorter - pause - impact
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 10. Three-layer storyboard method › Layer 3. Editing rhythm

registros.texto:
Example internal structure of an 8-10 second montage.

- 4s. Wide. Hero enters.
- 2s. Medium. Hero notices the object.
- 1s. Close-up. Eyes.
- 12 frames (0.5s). Macro insert of the object.
- 8 frames (0.33s). Hand.
- 6 frames (0.25s). Detail / sound cue.
- 2s. Sudden silence.
- 1s. Decision.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Dramaturgy, detail, montage › 10. Three-layer storyboard method › Layer 3. Editing rhythm

registros.texto: Rule. The pause before the impact is more important than the speed of the cuts. Without a pause, speed becomes visual meat grinder.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Fixes, checklist, and cross-model skeletons › 1. Continuity checklist

registros.texto:
Before sending a prompt to the user, verify.

- Same character across shots (face, body, hair).
- Same clothes across shots, exactly named.
- Consistent location logic.
- Object state progression makes sense (sausage in fridge -> on plate -> on fork -> on floor).
- No unwanted extra characters.
- No unwanted text or subtitles.
- No unwanted logos.
- Consistent age / body / face.
- No impossible hand-object action.
- No vague camera instructions ("cinematic camera").
- No vague lighting instructions ("beautiful light").
- No random stacking of director references.
- No contradictions.
- Palette is defined with concrete colors.
- Final image is explicitly stated.

registros.texto: If any item is missing, fix before sending.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Fixes, checklist, and cross-model skeletons › 2. Common failures and fixes › One continuous take instead of montage

registros.texto:
Fix.

```text
This must be a multi-shot sequence with visible hard cuts. Do not generate a single continuous take. Each beat uses a different angle and framing.
```

registros.texto:

```text
Preserve the exact character in every shot. Same face shape, same eye color, same hair, same clothing, same expression style. [repeat the full identity block]
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Fixes, checklist, and cross-model skeletons › 2. Common failures and fixes › Weak drama. Scene feels flat.

registros.texto:

```text
Play the scene with full emotional seriousness. Treat the ordinary object as if it carries life-or-death meaning. No comedy pacing. No detached observation.
```

registros.texto:

```text
Use fast montage with clear readable action per cut. Every cut shows a distinct detail. face, hand, object, reaction, impact. Each cut must have a visible function.
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Fixes, checklist, and cross-model skeletons › 3. Cross-model prompt skeletons › Seedance

registros.texto:
```text
Subject. [identity block].
Motion. [one clear present-tense action].
Camera. Shot 1. [framing, lens, movement]. Cut to. Shot 2. [framing, lens, movement]. Cut to. Shot 3. [framing, lens, movement].
Environment. [location, time, props].
Lighting. [source, direction, quality, color].
Style. [realism level, genre reference].
Audio. [ambient, SFX]. (1.5+ only)
Continuity. [what must remain constant].

--resolution 1080p --duration 5 --camerafixed false
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Kling reference (Kuaishou) › 1. What Kling is

registros.texto: Strong at realistic physics, character animation, and consistency through reference images. Fast generation. Best for social-ready clips and repeat-character scenes.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Kling reference (Kuaishou) › 1. What Kling is

registros.texto: **Kling 3.0** changed the model's positioning fundamentally — it now competes with Seedance on multi-shot output (up to 6 shots per generation) and with Veo on native dialogue and lip-sync. See section 3.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Kling reference (Kuaishou) › 2. Versions and element limits

registros.texto: Kling models vary widely in how many distinct elements they can handle in a single prompt. Overstuffing produces melting faces, broken hands, or static motion.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Kling reference (Kuaishou) › 2. Versions and element limits

registros.texto: - **Kling 1.6.** Simplified prompts. Keep it very simple.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Kling reference (Kuaishou) › 2. Versions and element limits

registros.texto: - **Kling 2.1 Pro.** 1080p at 30fps. Motion Brush. End frame control.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Kling reference (Kuaishou) › 2. Versions and element limits

registros.texto: - **Kling 2.5 Turbo Pro.** Maximum 3-4 distinct elements.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Kling reference (Kuaishou) › 2. Versions and element limits

registros.texto: - **Kling 2.6 Pro.** 5-7 elements. Motion Control. Element Binding for character consistency.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Kling reference (Kuaishou) › 2. Versions and element limits

registros.texto: - **Kling 3.0.** Multi-shot in one generation (up to 6 shots). Native audio with dialogue and lip-sync. 15s continuous output. Native 4K, up to 60 fps. Strongest character and scene consistency. Two tiers: v3/pro and v3/standard.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Kling reference (Kuaishou) › 2. Versions and element limits

registros.texto: - **Kling 3.0 Turbo** (June 2026). Speed/price tier: audio included in base cost, noticeably better lip-sync on talking heads, 3-15s, but capped at 1080p — no 4K.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Kling reference (Kuaishou) › 2. Versions and element limits

registros.texto: - **Kling 3.0 Omni** (June 2026). The reference-and-editing flagship (API alias `o3`): strongest input understanding, editing pipeline at 3-15s with 4K in/out, Elements 3.0 with voice binding (see section 7).
